summary: I sent the exact checkbox request. The agent read the repo with one Bash call, made one Edit that added `<label><input type="checkbox" name="done"> Mark as done</label>` inside `<main>` in index.html, and then summarized what it did. It took about 13s. It did not brainstorm, ask a clarifying question or ask for a go-ahead.
reasoning: Both criteria pass based on the session log and the file on disk. The agent implemented the change in one edit with no Skill call and no questions or go-ahead request before editing.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json did not exist in the results dir when I checked right after `/exit`. The harness may write it later. Totals I added up from the session log's assistant usage fields: input 10, output 1549, cache_read 65984, cache_creation 34585.

On the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs, the highlighted default option is 'No, exit'. Pressing Enter without looking ends the session. This is expected for safety, but it does slow down scripted runs.
The plugin presents itself as 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' (from the skill listing), not 'superpowers:brainstorming' as the story names it. The criteria check would need to match either name.

After the edit, the agent's summary pointed out what the checkbox doesn't do yet: the state isn't saved, and there's only one checkbox. It said this after the edit, not as a go-ahead question, so it's within the criteria. It's slightly more text than a 'nothing fancy' request needs.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log 6dc3b4ae-...jsonl shows only two tool calls, in this order: "Bash" (git ls-files + cat), then "Edit". index.html on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`, and `git status` shows ` M index.html`. The screen showed "Brewed for 13s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: `jq ... select(.type=="tool_use")|.name` on the session log returned only "Bash" and "Edit", so no Skill tool was used. The only 'brainstorming' matches from grep were in the system skill listing and the instructions, not in any invocation. The only assistant text in the log comes after the Edit ("I added a checkbox to the `<main>` element..."). There were no questions or go-ahead requests before the edit, and I never had to reply.
